paper.title_en: Neural and Tensor-Network Representations of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Cluster and Dipolar-cluster SPT States
paper.abstract_en: The $\mathbb Z_N$ cluster state is a paradigmatic example of symmetry-protected topological (SPT) order with $\mathbb Z_N\times\mathbb Z_N$ symmetry. We express its wavefunction and those of dipolar cluster states as a projector-based realization of correlator product states, which we dub the $P$-representation. The local projector $P$, also known as the copy tensor, can have multiple legs connecting a site to neighboring sites depending on the model and its deformations. We construct explicit wavefunctions of cluster and dipolar cluster states under deformation using the $P$-representation. The transition to the neural quantum state representations of the same state occurs by splitting the interaction matrices between $\mathbb{Z}_N$ spins into a pair of weight matrices. We derive these weight matrices explicitly for the cluster and dipolar cluster states, thus generalizing previous works on $\mathbb{Z}_2$ cluster states. The projector scheme then leads to the tensor product state (TPS) representation of the cluster-state wavefunctions. We benchmark the resulting TPS construction against conventional MPS representation using density-matrix renormalization group simulations and argue that the TPS could offer efficient representations for some modulated and deformed SPT states.
